title: About page portrait is a 515 KB PNG shown at 160 px
evidence: profile_kayjoyflowers.png is 800×800, 515 KB, displayed in a 160×160 circle. Lighthouse total page weight for /about.html: 1,043 KB, flagged by modern-image-formats and uses-responsive-images.
principle: Images should be delivered at roughly the size they are displayed (2× for sharp screens) in a modern format. Every extra 100 KB is noticeable on mobile data.
fix: Serve a 320×320 WebP copy from the site itself and keep the original for the share image.

title: Library page's largest image is lazy-loaded, delaying LCP to 3.5 s
evidence: Lighthouse (mobile, median of 3): /library.html LCP 3.50 s and audit lcp-lazy-loaded failed. Every other page: LCP 1.80–1.86 s.
principle: The browser waits to fetch lazy images until layout is known. The first visible image should load eagerly with high priority.
fix: Remove loading="lazy" from the first card image and add fetchpriority="high".

title: Quote attribution on dark bands fails colour contrast (2.31:1)
evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast: <cite> text #5F5866 on #2A1F2C = 2.31:1; WCAG AA needs 4.5:1. Affects the quote bands on the home, Fearlessly Unfuckwithable and Energetic Scans pages.
principle: Small text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 so it stays readable on phones outdoors and for low-vision readers.
fix: Give .band .quote cite a light tint of the band text colour.

title: No favicon: /favicon.ico returns 404 on every page
evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console on all six pages: 'Failed to load resource: 404' for /favicon.ico. No <link rel="icon"> in any page.
principle: Google shows the site icon next to results on mobile, and browsers show it in tabs and bookmarks. Without one the site looks unfinished and logs an error.
fix: Add a favicon (SVG plus PNG/ICO fallbacks and an Apple touch icon) and link it from every page.

title: Book cover tags declare the wrong shape (600×800 for a 600×600 image)
evidence: The cover image file is 600×600, but index.html, fearlessly-unfuckwithable.html and book.html set width="600" height="800". The browser reserves a portrait box, then the square image loads.
principle: width/height attributes tell the browser the aspect ratio before the image arrives. A wrong ratio causes layout jumps.

title: Library card images stop 52 px short of the card edge
evidence: Measured in Chromium at 390 px and 1280 px: card spans 124–367 px, image spans 126–313 px. The global img{max-width:100%} rule overrides the card image's full-bleed width.
principle: Visual polish signals care and trust, especially on a product listing.

title: One square book cover is the share image for every page
evidence: Before the patch there were no og:image tags at all. The patch uses the 600×600 book cover for home, Library, Energetic Scans and Privacy. Large share cards are 1200×630 (1.91:1), so a square image is cropped, and the Energetic Scans preview shows the book.
principle: The share preview is the first thing people see in Instagram DMs, Facebook, iMessage and WhatsApp. It should match the page and be the right shape.
fix: Make a 1200×630 share image per key page in the site's own colours and fonts, using only existing headlines, and declare og:image:width, og:image:height and og:image:alt.

title: The Library page is thin (123 words) and the coming-soon titles have no descriptions
evidence: Audit word count 123. Seven collections are listed by title and format only. Search and answer engines have nothing to quote about Medicine Woman, Energetic Alchemist, Jailbreak and the rest.
principle: Answer engines cite pages that answer a question in a sentence or two. A list of titles answers nothing.
fix: Kay to write one or two lines per collection in her own words. Not written by the audit, so no copy is invented.

title: The flagship page has no answer-first section or FAQ
evidence: /fearlessly-unfuckwithable.html answers 'what is it, what's in the bundle, what does it cost' across separate sections, but has no short, quotable answers to the questions buyers ask (format, delivery, currency, is it therapy).
principle: FAQ blocks with visible questions and short answers are among the most quoted formats in AI answers. Every answer must be true and already supported by the page.
fix: A draft FAQ built only from facts already on the page is in drafts/fearlessly-unfuckwithable-faq-draft.md. It is NOT applied and needs Kay's approval.

title: Library hero has no button
evidence: The first screen of /library.html is a headline and introduction only. The first card's Explore button is just below it.
principle: A clear next step in the first screen helps visitors who arrive from search.
fix: Accepted as is: the card grid starts straight after the hero and the flagship card has its own button. Revisit if Kay adds collection descriptions.

title: Render-blocking font and style sheets
evidence: Lighthouse render-blocking-resources on every page: the Google Fonts CSS and styles.css. Mobile FCP is about 1.8 s (simulated slow 4G). Performance scores are already 90–99.
principle: CSS blocks first paint. Fonts already use display=swap, so text is never invisible.
fix: Accepted. Self-hosting fonts would save one connection but changes the privacy policy's Google Fonts disclosure. Recommend reconsidering later.

title: Short browser cache lifetime (10 minutes)
evidence: Response header cache-control: max-age=600 on all files.
principle: Longer caching speeds up repeat visits.
fix: Hosting limitation: GitHub Pages sets this and it cannot be changed. Versioned file names (styles.css?v=6) are already used, which is the right pattern.

title: Security headers cannot be set; HTTP→HTTPS not testable from here
evidence: GitHub Pages does not allow custom headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options). Verified: www.kayjoyflowers.online → 301 → apex; kay639.github.io/kayjoyflowers-site/ → 301 → apex; HTTPS serves a valid certificate. Plain http:// could not be tested because the audit environment blocks port 80.
principle: Headers harden a site, but a static site with no logins or forms on the public pages has little attack surface.
fix: Kay to confirm 'Enforce HTTPS' is ticked in GitHub → Settings → Pages. Headers would need a CDN such as Cloudflare in front, which is not recommended now.

title: Beacons checkout pages can't be verified automatically
evidence: shop.beacons.ai returns a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403) to scripts and headless browsers. The two Beacons product IDs are consistent across the site: 43241ff0 is the book (US$33) and eaf21d86 the bundle (US$77). The three buy.stripe.com links and the billing portal return HTTP 200. The connected Stripe account has no payment links, so the scan links belong to a different Stripe account and their prices could not be read by API.
principle: A checkout link that silently points to the wrong product loses sales and trust.
fix: Manual click-through by Kay after deploy (checklist in the after-report). The audit treats these links as 'unverified', not 'passed'.

title: Decision needed: robots.txt allows AI training crawlers as well as AI search
evidence: The applied patch allows GPTBot and Google-Extended, which collect content for AI model training, as well as the AI search crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot) that power citations.
principle: Blocking training crawlers does not stop citations in ChatGPT Search or Perplexity. Allowing them is a content-licensing choice, not an SEO requirement.
fix: Kept as the patch set it. Kay decides: to opt out of training only, change GPTBot, Google-Extended and ClaudeBot to 'Disallow: /'.
